------------------------------------------------------------------------

One of the great draws of Korean food is the ubiquitous and abundant offering of *banchan*, or side dishes. It is not uncommon for these complimentary offerings—a well-fermented kimchi, a seasoned mountain herb, or a simple braised dish—to match or even surpass the main dish on the table. A restaurant may offer them merely as a bonus, but for the diner, they often become the real reason to return.

In life, we tend to fixate on our primary goals. We push forward toward the big achievements, often setting aside the small, quiet things we consider secondary—assuming they will still be waiting for us once the "main thing" is finished.

Yet, it is so often those seemingly unimportant, non-urgent side items that ultimately define the quality of our days. The spontaneous conversation, the quiet detour, the small gesture kept alive over time—these are the *banchan* of living. What begins on the periphery of our attention can quietly become the center of our nourishment, reminding us that the main course was never the whole story.

Recently, as we were riding toward a mountain location two and a half hours away, the driver mentioned how we had once housed his family while they were looking for permanent housing.

I wanted to acknowledge his words with a thoughtful response, but I couldn't remember doing it.

The event was significant to him and he remembered it 22 years later, regretably it had registered in my memory.

What felt like a small, expected gesture had become a part of his life story.

Likewise, it is those seemingly unimportant, non-urgent acts that make the real difference in this life.

What we offer on the side can quietly become the main thing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

As we were riding towards our mountain location 2.5 hours away, the driver mentioned how we housed him and his family while they were looking for their permanent housing.

I wanted to recognize the fact and provide a response, however, I couldn't remember if we ever did.

The event was significant to him and he remembered but I had forgotten.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
